ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, and signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Global Affairs Canada autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Magnitsky Act, and PEP databases (including domestic foreign royal and senior official networks). Screening must be performed prior to filing, refreshed on transactional triggers and at least annually, and logged for five years. Positive hits require immediate escalation to the Chief Anti-Money Laundering Officer and mandatory FINTRAC Terrorist Property Report or Suspicious Transaction Report under PCMLTFA, as applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services (BC Registries) online portal: https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca and OneStop Business Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filing language is English; the legal name of a BC LP must be expressed in Latin characters. A non-Latin script name may be used descriptively, but the registered legal name must be a transliterated Latin-script version. The name must end in 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'LP', or the French equivalent 'Société en commandite' where bilingual filing is used, and must not be misleading under Business Corporations Act Regulation, B.C. Reg. 14/2004, s. 5.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name reservation may be reconsidered by submitting a written Request for Reconsideration to the BC Registrar of Companies, Attention: Name Review Unit, within 30 days of the rejection notice. The request must include a complete explanation, supporting marks, evidence of consents from relevant regulators, and a corrected name search. The Registrar will issue a written decision within 21 days. If the reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 56 days before expiry if the corporate structure and intended jurisdiction remain unchanged.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted as the registered office in BC provided it is a dedicated physical street address within British Columbia at which process may be served during regular business hours and the registered office service provider is licensed or engaged as an agent. A virtual office does not, by itself, create sufficient commercial substance; for ISIC 5820 PC/console digital publishing, the partnership should maintain demonstrable operational substance through contracts, server logs, professional support, or local staff to preserve pass-through tax benefits and avoid Canadian-source PE characterization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is low, below 2% annually for a clean digital-services LP; the BC registrar may conduct unannounced inspection where there is material non-compliance, mail-return, or evidence that the registered office is not staffed as required.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 45, ss. 7, 8, 9, 10 (registration and duties); Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, s. 2; Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, c. 57 as to ancillary company proceedings; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 for partnership taxation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia, Victoria, BC
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) and Certificate of Limited Partnership issued by the Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for a British Columbia limited partnership; limited partners may contribute cash, services or property as set out in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is imposed by BC Registries.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a meeting of the general partner of [Limited Partnership Name] held on [Date], the following resolutions were approved unanimously: 1) the subscriptions of the initial limited partners to the partnership capital, as reflected in the Schedule of Contributions, are accepted and the general partner's interest is subscribed in full; 2) the Registered Office of the Limited Partnership in British Columbia is fixed as [Address] for service and statutory filing purposes; 3) [Representative] is appointed as general partner's managing representative to oversee day-to-day operations and filings under the Limited Partnership Act; 4) [Agent] is appointed to obtain GST/HST, PST, municipal licences and future amendments; 5) the partners authorize the general partner to execute ancillary documents and open bank accounts. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-approval of the Limited Partnership Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Name Request service through BC Registries Corporate Online. Select 'Limited Partnership', enter the proposed name and up to two alternatives, and pay the prescribed name reservation fee by credit card. The system performs a search against existing BC corporate and limited partnership names. After approval, a Name Reservation Certificate is issued and remains valid for 56 days.
required_dossiers: List of up to three proposed partnership names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is refused, the Registrar will state the reason. File a revised name request or request reconsideration within 21 days, attaching evidence of consent or trademark distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Declaration and Obtain Certificate of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP-1, Declaration of Limited Partnership, in English or French. Include the approved partnership name, a registered address in British Columbia, a mailing address, full legal names and addresses of every general partner and limited partner, and the condition that the partnership has no more than X limited partners if preferred. Submit the declaration through BC Corporate Online and pay the filing fee by credit card. The Registrar reviews the declaration and issues the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1)
Limited Partnership Agreement (for records; not filed)
List of general and limited partners with addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected for formality, correct the discrepancy and resubmit. If an error appears after registration, the partners must file a supplementary or amending declaration under ss. 8 and 9 of the Limited Partnership Act; any adverse registration can be remedied by a court order for rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Tax Accounts with Canada Revenue Agency and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and British Columbia Ministry of Finance—Taxpayer Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO), request a Business Number for the limited partnership for GST/HST, payroll and any other related program accounts. Register a BC PST account via the BC Tax Services online system if the partnership makes taxable retail sales in British Columbia, such as physical game merchandise or other in-BC supplies. Each program account requires the partnership's legal name, Certificate of Limited Partnership, and principal place of business.
required_dossiers: Legal names and business addresses of partners
CRA Business Registration Online application confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or BC Ministry of Finance indicates non-disclosure or mismatched name, submit an information correction within 30 days. If accounts are assigned late, request cancellation ab initio or adjust penalty by showing due diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Local Zoning Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Specific municipal business licence office, e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence Office or City of Burnaby Licence Office, under the BC Community Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a physical operating premise (if any) or clearly confirm a fully digital activity with no storefront. If a street-level or office address is used for business in the city, apply for a Municipal Business Licence through the city's eService or counter service. Provide proof of registered office, general partner contact data, and a short description of the business. The licence is renewed annually and may require a production or home-occupation endorsement.
required_dossiers: Lease, ownership document, or landlord consent for the business location
General partner identification and contact information
Activity description (software and digital game publishing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipal licence is denied, seek review before the local Administrative Appeals Board within 14 days of service. Failure to obtain a licence may result in a fine; cure by immediate application and payment of retroactive fee if not exempt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WorkSafeBC Occupational Health and Safety Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the limited partnership employs any worker in British Columbia, register as an employer with WorkSafeBC. Complete the online Employer Registration application, calculate audited payroll, and provide the occupational classification code for software publishing (omit if inapplicable). The account covers workers' compensation and occupational health and safety obligations, including required first aid and incident reporting.
required_dossiers: Projected annual payroll and remuneration estimate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafeBC assigns a higher premium classification, request a reconsideration within 45 days and provide job descriptions. If registration is required but not completed, late filing penalties can be mitigated by prompt submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing board is applicable to pure digital software and game publishing. For any physical office use, the local municipal business licence office and the provincial Business Regulations and Consumer Protection Branch provide relevant routine permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required—no sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating licence; if office premises are used, a Municipal Business Licence may be required under the Community Charter and local bylaw.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy—Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt—the business consists of digital publishing with no physical construction, extraction, land alteration, or industrial process triggering a Comprehensive Study or Assessment under the Environmental Assessment Act or the Environmental Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process discharges exist. In-house operations must, at minimum, maintain any negligible municipal sewer discharges below accepted thresholds; no VOC, particulate, or hazardous waste are generated by the licensed software publishing activity. Any outsourced data hosting is subject to the host's environmental permits and certifications.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a physical office is established, obtain a fire safety inspection certificate and BC Building Code compliance clearance for occupancy loads and means of egress. WorkSafeBC registration and basic occupational first aid coverage are required for employees. No hazardous substance storage is anticipated for digital publishing. Structural load and electrical safety inspections must be secured for any server room or specialized IT infrastructure installed on premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - ADMINISTERS GST/HST and the federal Business Number (BN); CRA My Business Account portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch - ADMINISTERS BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and employer health tax; BC Tax Central / eTaxBC portal at https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Register the limited partnership with BC Registries (under the Partnership Act) via BC Corporate Online, or file an extra-provincial LP registration if the LP was formed outside BC. STEP 2: Request the federal 15-character Business Number (BN) with program accounts (GST/HST = RT account) through the BC Registries one-stop filing or by submitting CRA Form RC1; the LP itself is a 'person' for GST/HST purposes and holds its own separate registration, not the individual partners. STEP 3: Open the BC PST account with the Consumer Taxation Branch if the LP makes taxable sales of goods or digital services to BC consumers; no BC PST small-supplier exemption applies. STEP 4: Register for the BC employer health tax if BC payroll exceeds CAD 500,000 annually. Foreign partners are not prevented from forming or owning a BC LP; a non-resident partner with Canadian-source income must file Form T2046/NR6 processes and a Canadian agent for service of process is recommended.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not use a US-style 'check-the-box' system; the BC LP is statutorily transparent: income/loss allocates to partners under ITA s. 96. Available elections include: contribution rollover to the partnership under ITA s. 97(2); successor/continuance rollovers under ITA s. 98(1); commercial-cost-allocation under ETA s. 272.1 for GST; joint closely-related-person election under ETA s. 156 (streams GST on inter-party supplies); transfer-of-business election under ETA s. 167; and hybrid-mismatch protections under ITA Part XVI.1 and s. 18.4 which limit otherwise deductible payments where the payee treats them as non-taxable under a foreign hybrid instrument or entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST (single-stage goods and services tax, 5%) plus British Columbia PST (7%) - separate non-harmonized taxes; combined headline consumer rate for taxable goods/digital goods in BC is 12%, but GST and PST are levied independently and PST does not apply to most B2B services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - ETA small-supplier annual threshold (worldwide taxable supplies over four consecutive calendar quarters, excluding supply of financial services and capital assets of the business). A non-resident supplier of digital services who is a 'distributor' or uses a 'specified platform operator' has NO small-supplier relief effective July 1, 2021; BC PST has no registration threshold for vendors making taxable sales to BC consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, digital stamping or CRA API pre-approval exists at federal or BC level. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records (PDF, EDI, JSON/XML, PEPPOL/Factur-X where voluntarily implemented); the 6-year retention rule under ETA s. 286(1) applies. Invoices issued by the LP must show the BN/RT account, date, supplier and recipient identity, and GST charged; Steam and PlayStation payout statements constitute acceptable underlying records for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The LP may apply 0% GST under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 of the Excise Tax Act to royalties/licence fees for video-game copyright supplied to non-resident, non-GST-registered recipients (Valve/Steam, PlayStation/Sony Interactive Entertainment) where the intangible property is exploited wholly outside Canada (use-enjoyment test; markets outside Canada). Royalties attributable to Canadian end-user downloads are taxable at 5% GST and will normally be collected and remitted by the platform operator under the digital-economy deemed-supply rules, avoiding double collection. Offshore publishing, localization, or IT-support services to non-residents may qualify for zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 or Part VII where the recipient is a non-resident and no service is performed in Canada for Canadian enjoyment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13 or ACI/eManifest) - required ONLY for physical game media/disc exports; not applicable to digital downloads transferred via Steam/PlayStation networks
Valve Steam publisher payout reports and Sony PlayStation Store royalty statements showing title, contract period, territorial sales, and net remittable amounts
Executed publishing and licence agreements with Valve Corporation, Warner Bros./PlayStation, or other non-resident platform operators delineating territorial rights and royalty basis
Commercial invoices or digital delivery memos evidencing the electronic transfer of the game code/IP to foreign licensees
Inward remittance and wire-transfer records (bank statements, FX conversion reports) proving non-resident payment and CAD settlement
GST/HST returns and supporting working papers reconciling the zero-rated portion declared on each period's return (CRA GST/HST Memorandum Series 8-3 documentation standards)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits apply the 'place of use' and 'principal purpose' tests; any retail sale downloaded by a Canadian consumer that was improperly zero-rated triggers reassessment of 5% GST plus 7% BC PST on the Canadian portion. Penalties: gross-negligence penalty under ETA s. 285 (up to 25% of net tax) and ITA s. 163(2) (up to 50% of the tax), compounded daily interest under ETA s. 280, and removal of the normal 4-year reassessment window under ETA s. 298(7) where misrepresentation is established. Deliberate fraud exposes partners to joint and several liability under ETA ss. 272.1/323 and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under ETA s. 327 (fines of 50%-200% of evaded tax plus up to 5 years imprisonment on indictment), plus possible Steam/PlayStation platform de-listing and reputational harm.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); exchange-control administrative authority rests with the Minister of Finance, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); prudential banking supervision is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction: the Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts, with no exchange-control approvals, surrender obligations, or repatriation restrictions for trade settlements, capital injections, dividends, interest, or partnership profit distributions. For a BC limited partnership, a non-resident partner's share of income may be freely remitted, subject to statutory Part XIII withholding tax of 25% under the Income Tax Act, treaty-reduced where applicable (e.g., Canada-US Treaty: 0-15% on interest and royalties, 5-15% on dividends). The Investment Canada Act imposes a net-benefit review only on specified acquisitions of control of a Canadian business, not on passive LP interests. The principal operational frictions are reporting and verification: cross-border currency movements exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to CBSA/FINTRAC; electronic funds transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 are recorded by financial institutions; and FINTRAC's customer due diligence (full-CDR) framework requires identification and verification of every individual or entity holding 25% or more of the partnership before account opening (PCMLTFA Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada repealed its foreign-exchange surrender regime under the Exchange Control Act in 1951. Exporters and digital-service publishers (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210) may retain 100% of export proceeds in CAD or foreign-currency accounts with no statutory conversion ratio, holding period, or surrender deadline. Steam (Valve Corp.) and PlayStation Store (Sony Interactive Entertainment) USD payouts may be held indefinitely in a US-dollar subsidiary ledger at a Schedule I bank or remitted to offshore accounts without Bank of Canada authorization. For GST/HST purposes, exports of digital game licences qualify as zero-rated supplies under the Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, Section 9, provided the partnership retains platform payout statements as export evidence; the platform operators remain responsible for GST/HST registration and collection on sales to Canadian consumers.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM - usable as a secondary operational rail but not a substitute for a Schedule I bank. Wise (Wise Payments Ltd., FINTRAC-registered MSB with local partner banking) and Payoneer (Payoneer Inc., FINTRAC MSB) can receive USD payout rails from Valve and Sony, convert to CAD, and support Steam ACH and PlayStation B2B disbursements; both are acceptable for vendor payments and freelance royalties. Legal constraints: (a) neither is an OSFI-regulated deposit-taking institution, so balances are not CDIC-insured and must be swept to the primary bank; (b) offshore EU/UK EMI e-money licences do not confer membership in Payments Canada's ACSS or Lynx clearing systems, preventing same-day domestic CAD clearing and SWIFT domestic branch routing; (c) Schedule I banks will require disclosure of all payment-processor accounts as linked entities at onboarding; and (d) the partnership's GST/HST and export-evidence trail is more robust with a Canadian bank settlement record. Do not hold capital escrow or fiduciary trust balances through EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a BC-registered limited partnership, all Schedule I banks in practice mandate a physical or live-video KYC interview for the authorized signatory (normally the General Partner's managing member) at initial account opening; fully remote 'no-touch' opening is not offered for LPs with non-resident limited partners. RBC requires an in-branch sign-off unless the GP is a Canadian federally-registered corporation with more than two years of operating history, in which case enhanced remote video verification may be accepted; TD permits video KYC for BC LPs provided the GP presents government-issued ID live and the LP agreement is notarized; BMO allows remote opening for arm's-length LPs that already hold a qualifying prior banking relationship. Passive non-resident limited partners are not required to appear if each 25%+ beneficial owner is identified and verified under FINTRAC full-CDR rules. The partnership must deliver its BC Limited Partnership registration certificate, complete LP agreement, capital-call notices, and CRA Business Number. Foreign-owned LPs should budget four to eight weeks for underwriting and final account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident limited partners (trust, foundation, or corporate-veil ownership) flagged by the FINTRAC full-CDR 25%+ beneficial-ownership screen and the BC Land Owner Transparency Registry cross-check.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Fully executed LP agreement and BC Form 2 / registration confirmation; (ii) beneficial-ownership waterfall chart mapping each 25%+ partner to a real individual; (iii) certified passports and three months of bank statements for each UBO; (iv) tax residency certificates from the partner's jurisdiction; (v) negative-media and sanctions-screen evidence (OFAC, UN, EU, OSFI lists); (vi) a sworn passive-investor declaration confirming non-participation in management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical nexus: digital-publisher IP revenues with zero Canadian employees and sales exclusively through Steam and PlayStation platform stores, triggering the bank's high-risk 'virtual asset / non-face-to-face business' category.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Valve Steamworks Publisher Agreement and Sony PlayStation Partner Developer Agreement; (ii) twelve months of platform payout statements from Steam and PlayStation financial dashboards; (iii) CIPO copyright and trademark registration certificates; (iv) co-publishing and sub-licensing agreements; (v) evidence of a registered BC office or registered-agency address; (vi) CRA Business Number and GST/HST registration confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity outbound wires to numerous overseas development studios (royalty waterfall payments), flagged by transaction monitoring as possible structuring or unlicensed money transmission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Royalty schedule and revenue-share calculation per title; (ii) executed development, localization, and art contracts with KYC passports of each contractor; (iii) IP-assignment agreements and escrow release conditions; (iv) the LP's written transaction-monitoring policy (e.g., dual approval and contract verification for aggregate wires above CAD 200,000); (v) quarterly cash-flow forecasts tied to platform sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USD payouts from Valve and Sony with payment narratives such as 'Game Software / USD EFT' that may be misclassified as cross-border asset transfers, or OFAC/sanctions concern regarding Steam wallets accessible in restricted territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Treasury due-diligence profile on Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment LLC; (ii) jurisdiction-residency filter report demonstrating no sanctioned-country consumption within the LP's controlled catalogue; (iii) KYC files on all platform-linked developer studios; (iv) the LP's published Trade Sanctions and Export Compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection (above CAD 1 million) from a foreign partner in a higher-risk jurisdiction followed by rapid intercompany disbursements to third parties, indicating possible layering or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Capital-call notice and drawdown schedule approved by the GP; (ii) source-of-wealth documentation for the contributing partner (audited financial statements, sale-purchase agreements, or exit proceeds records); (iii) notarized Deed of Capital Contribution; (iv) the LP's treasury and cash-flow model with projected burn rate; (v) a bank reference letter from the partner's originating bank, plus SWIFT cover details confirming the economic purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all partner capital calls via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV where intermediated) into the LP's CAD or USD account at the Schedule I bank, using: Field 50K for the ordering partner, Field 59 for the LP beneficiary with legal name and BC registration number, and Field 70 remittance narrative: 'CAPITAL CALL NO. [x] per LP Agreement dated [yyyy-mm-dd]; BC LP Registration No. [number]; CRA BN [number]; UBO [name]'. Use ISO 20022 External Purpose Code 'INTC' (intercompany payment) or 'INVE' (investment) as mapped by the receiving bank's online purpose-code menu; never use gift, salary, or personal-transfer codes. The bank verifies that (a) the beneficiary name matches the BC Registry, (b) the ordering party appears on the LP's approved partner list, and (c) no FINTRAC EFT reportable threshold (CAD 10,000) is circumvented. For injections above CAD 50,000, the bank will typically request the supporting capital-call notice, proof of the LP agreement, and source-of-funds documentation; escrow/holdback balances must be labelled 'Trust/Escrow' and maintained as segregated ledgers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) Inbound platform payouts - Steam (Valve Corp.) wires USD via ACH/SWIFT to the LP's USD subsidiary account under the Steam Payout schedule; PlayStation Store (Sony Interactive Entertainment) remits USD or CAD monthly via SWIFT MT103; proceeds are converted to CAD through the bank's FX desk at the daily CAD/USD rate, or retained in USD for hedged disbursements. (2) Royalty payments to international developers are executed by SWIFT MT103 (direct beneficiary account) with purpose code 'TRAD' or 'SUPP' and Field 70 stating 'Royalty under [Title] Publishing Agreement dated [x]'; MT202 COV is used for correspondent transit. (3) Domestic CAD payments clear through Payments Canada ACSS for low-value batch, and Lynx RTGS for high-value wires with finality under the Payment Clearing and Settlement Act. (4) Commercial documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600) are reserved for physical-goods co-production (collector's editions, merchandise) and standby LCs for platform-advance performance guarantees; Interac e-Transfer and P2P rails are prohibited for trade settlement due to FINTRAC large-value monitoring and auditability requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX outright forwards (1-12 months) executed under the bank's ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and FX Addendum, hedged against forecast Steam and PlayStation USD sales with IFRS 9 designation files.
CAD/USD European-style OTC options and zero-cost collar structures for converting USD platform proceeds, exempt from central-clearing mandates under Canadian derivatives rules.

CAD/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing an independent fixing, permissible for hedging revenues receivable in soft or emerging-market currencies (RUB, TRY, ARS, and regional Steam wallet flows) where deliverability constraints apply.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) for medium-term matching of partnership capital liabilities against USD-denominated platform receivables, executed under ISDA 2002 CSA.
Exchange-traded CME CAD/USD futures and options (CME ticker 6C) providing transparent, margin-efficient hedges available without commercial-bank credit-line expansion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registry (Service BC, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary of the limited partnership's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late filing penalty is prescribed by the Partnership Act; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to strike the limited partnership from the register, resulting in loss of limited liability protection and legal incapacity to carry on business until reinstatement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and Allocation Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Later of March 31 or six months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, due March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD $25 per day from the due date for up to 100 days, maximum CAD $2,500; repeated or gross negligent late filing may result in additional penalties and administrative prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit is imposed on a BC limited partnership solely by the Limited Partnership Act. A mandatory audit may arise under the partnership agreement, investor rights, securities law exemptions, or lender covenants; otherwise an audit is optional for internal and tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS under CPA Canada Handbook Part 1 for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE under CPA Canada Handbook Part 2 is available for Canadian private enterprises, including limited partnerships. The choice is governed by the partnership agreement and applicable professional standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual public confirmation of UBO information is required solely for a BC limited partnership; however, the partnership must maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control, update it within 30 days of any transfer of a partnership interest, and preserve records reflecting current limited and general partner holdings. Such register may be required to be disclosed to the Registrar upon demand or in compliance with anti-money laundering obligations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD $35 to $500 per year (approximately USD $25 to $370) depending on registered office and corporate agent service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD $5,000 to $15,000 (approximately USD $3,700 to $11,000) for a small-to-medium PC and console game publishing limited partnership

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate rate: federal 15% plus British Columbia 12%; the LP itself is fiscally transparent, so tax is imposed on corporate partners at their applicable rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners can claim the federal small business deduction plus the BC small business tax rate, producing a combined 11% rate on the first C$500,000 of eligible active business income allocated from the LP. Video-game publishing royalties are not automatically eligible for the BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit unless qualifying design/development activity is carried on in BC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (CRA) filed via CRA My Business Account or an approved software/EFILE service provider
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the end of the LP's fiscal period; the general partner must also ensure every non-resident limited partner receives its T5013 allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, business number (BN), CRA program account, jurisdiction of formation, fiscal year-end, principal business activity (NAICS 511210).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every non-resident partner and each partner's province/foreign country of residence; use the foreign address field and record non-resident partner percentages.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Steam/PlayStation Store publishing operations, royalty/licensing income, direct costs, operating expenses, and net income/loss for the partnership period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify Canadian-source income and foreign-source income so non-resident partners can determine Part I taxability and treaty issues.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advertising, platform/commissions, software royalties, development cost reimbursement, administrative expenses, and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold no Part XIII tax on partnership allocations; the LP's deductions should be supported by invoices and transfer pricing documentation if paid to non-resident affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 3 - Allocation of Income or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner name, CRA BN or TR/SS number, residency status, percentage share, allocated income/loss, and provincial allocation factor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations to non-resident corporate partners remain taxable in Canada if derived from carrying on business in Canada; do not treat them as dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete T5013 returns are information-return defaults exposed to ITA s.162(7) penalties (per-day administrative penalties, with higher amounts for gross negligence) and s.163(2) penalty of 50% of any understated tax caused by false statements or omissions.
